title: Revisiting Local PageRank Estimation on Undirected Graphs: Simple and Optimal

problem.claim: Estimate the PageRank score of an arbitrary target node in an undirected graph with small relative error and high success probability.

gap.claim: The previously best upper bound was O(log n ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)) and relied on a significantly more complex algorithm and analysis.

contributions.claim: BackMC is a simple algorithm for local PageRank estimation in undirected graphs that provides accurate estimates with small relative error and high success probability.
BackMC has worst-case computational complexity O(1/dmin ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)).
The paper establishes a matching lower bound of Ω(1/dmin ⋅ min(dt, m1/2)) for any algorithm solving local PageRank estimation.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors present BackMC as a simple and optimal algorithm and claim an improvement over the prior upper bound by a factor of Θ(log n/dmin).

author_reported_evidence.claim: On various large-scale real-world and synthetic graphs, BackMC consistently shows superior performance in the reported experiments.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper proposes BackMC for local PageRank estimation under accuracy and success-probability requirements.
It gives a worst-case complexity bound parameterized by the minimum graph degree and target-node degree.
It compares BackMC with the prior upper bound and reports a factor improvement with simpler algorithmic and analytical structure.
It establishes a matching lower bound to support theoretical optimality.
It reports experiments on real-world and synthetic graphs showing superior performance.

source_observation.claim: The reported algorithm improves the prior complexity bound while using a simpler algorithm.

interpretation.claim: When a problem has a complex prior solution, simplifying the method can coincide with better worst-case efficiency.

application.claim: Evaluate proposed algorithmic improvements jointly on complexity and structural simplicity rather than on either dimension alone.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the same simplicity or efficiency holds outside undirected-graph local PageRank estimation.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify BackMC's algorithmic steps or analysis.
The abstract does not provide experimental settings, datasets, baselines, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not state the precise accuracy and success-probability parameters.
